newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS: Forward supply worries gas oil.
newsitem.headline: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS: Forward supply worries gas oil.

text.p: Gas oil swaps were lower in Singapore around midday on Wednesday amid worries about forward supplies, while other products were also weaker.
The forward gas oil market was weaker due to the expected arrival of several arbitrage cargoes from the U.S. West Coast in late December and January, traders said.
The East-West diesel arbitrage has swung strongly to favor Asian imports in recent weeks as European and U.S. diesel prices have tumbled.
The November/December gas oil spread was a wide 50/60 cents, out from 30/40 cents last week, with Q1 gas oil offered at $28.20 per barrel.
November swaps were last quoted at $29.60/$29.70, down from $29.70/$29.80 late Tuesday, brokers said.
Traders said the weaker tone was in line with the crude market despite NYMEX heating oil recovering its New York losses on the after-hours ACCESS system.
December heating oil fell 0.53 cent to 65.42 cents a gallon in New York but rebounded to last trade at 65.95 cents on ACCESS.
December NYMEX crude lost 15 cents to close at $22.64 a barrel and was last traded at $22.63.
Jet fuel is under some selling pressure because Japanese buying for the winter has yet to emerge in a big way. December was offered at $30.10, down about 10 cents from late Tuesday.
The November regrade was quoted unchanged in a wide range of 10/40 cents.
Fuel oil swaps were quoted down at midday with November called at $115.25/$116.25 per tonne from Tuesday's $116.00/$116.50 and December was at $115.25/$116.00, brokers said.
Naphtha was notionally indicated at $21.60/$21.90, down from Monday's close of $21.70/$21.95.
